page: Amazon Web Services r5a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The server is configured with 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes zero GPUs and no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate compute and memory speeds consistent with earlier AMD EPYC architectures. The instance scored 724.0 on Geekbench single-core and 2909.0 on multi-core tests, placing processing capacity in the lower quartile of tested cloud servers. Similarly, stress-ng yielded 590.99 for single-core and 2360.55 for multi-core compute. Memory bandwidth testing recorded 21.56 GB/s for large-block read operations and 11.76 GB/s for writes. While vector calculation performance is constrained due to the absence of AVX-512 extensions, hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions yield a standard PassMark encryption score of 6464.01.

The hardware configuration provides high RAM density relative to core count, presenting an economical footprint for applications where memory capacity outweighs raw CPU execution speeds. Potential operational tradeoffs include the absence of integrated NVMe storage and modest network bandwidth. Amazon Web Services r5a.2xlarge is functional for memory-heavy environments including in-memory data caches, mid-scale relational database engines, and routine data extraction, transformation, and loading pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r5a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, allocating 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, depending entirely on network-attached block storage, with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Empirical benchmarks indicate modest single-thread and memory throughput, scoring 724.0 in Geekbench single-core and 21.56 GB/s in uncached large-block reads, while PassMark encryption achieves average throughput. The instance trades per-core compute speed for high memory capacity at an efficient hardware tier. This profile makes the instance suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand cutting-edge CPU performance, including Redis caching tiers, relational database servers, and batch ETL jobs.
